senses.zh: 领悟力强的；富有洞察力的
senses.en: able to understand, or showing that you understand, what a situation or person is really like
examples: We are always looking for more interesting and [[insightful]] ideas to share with our readers.

senses.en: a balance between different people, groups, or forces that compete with each other, so that none is stronger than the others and the situation is not likely to change suddenly
examples: The point at which the solid and the liquid are in [[equilibrium]] is called the freezing point.

senses.en: completely and only
examples: The management committee decided to close the museum [[purely]] because it cost too much to run.

senses.en: a situation in which it is very difficult to decide what to do, because all the choices seem equally good or equally bad
examples: The [[dilemma]] over human cloning lies at the heart of the ethical choices facing society.

senses.en: very good, enjoyable, or unusual, and worth remembering
examples: If you want to catch and save this [[memorable]] event in your life, bring your camera with you.

senses.en: widely accepted and used for a long time; traditional in style or idea
examples: Adam Smith is considered one of the founders of [[classical]] economics.

senses.en: (only before noun) shared or made by every member of a group or society
examples: I think it's our [[collective]] responsibility to create an environment for future generations to be even more successful.

senses.en: health and happiness
examples: Biological scientists have to consider the balance between human health and animal [[welfare]] as they push forward the frontiers of research.

senses.en: a story, painting, etc. in which the events and characters represent ideas or teach a moral lesson
examples: The book is a kind of [[allegory]] of Latin American history.

senses.en: impossible to see
examples: This sophisticated technology allows scientists to find things that are [[invisible]] to the naked eye.

senses.zh: 灾难性的；以失败告终的
senses.en: very bad, or ending in failure
examples: In some cases, lowering interest rates could have [[disastrous]] consequences for the economy.

senses.en: sb. who goes into houses, shops, etc. to steal things
examples: A number of [[burglars]] broke into the gallery and stole dozens of priceless paintings.

senses.en: say that you believe sb. is guilty of a crime or of doing sth. bad
examples: No one could ever [[accuse]] this government of not caring about the poor.

senses.en: the crime of stealing money or things from a bank, shop, etc., esp. using violence
examples: The gang (犯罪团伙) admitted they had committed four recent bank [[robberies]].

senses.en: admit, esp. to the police, that you have done sth. wrong or illegal
examples: Gabriele [[confessed]] to leaking copies of the documents to the press because he wanted to expose the "evil and corruption" in the company.

senses.en: (fml.) the best or most suitable
examples: They insist their business idea is [[optimal]] and will be wildly acceptable to customers.

senses.en: being in a better situation, if or after sth. happens
examples: You'd be [[better]] off living on your own than quarreling all the time with your dad.

senses.en: sth. that has the same value, purpose, job, etc. as sth. else
examples: Is there a French word that is the exact [[equivalent]] of the English word "home"?

senses.en: measured or judged by how similar or different it is to sth. else; relative
examples: After living in poverty for most of his lifetime, he spent his last few years in [[comparative]] comfort.

senses.zh: 散发，发出（气、热、光、声音等）
senses.en: send out gas, heat, light, sound, etc.
examples: The machine will [[emit]] a noisy sound when you press the red button.

senses.en: the fact that sb. is not doing anything
examples: The city council was accused of [[inaction]] on the parking problem of the city.

senses.en: (curriculum vitae) a short written document that lists your education and previous jobs, which you send to employers when you are looking for a job
examples: Applicants interested in applying for the position should submit their [[CVs]] no later than February 15.

senses.en: involve sth. as a necessary part or result
examples: The job of a dance teacher [[entails]] teaching students the technique and performance of dance movements.

senses.en: the fact of not using time, money, energy, etc. in the best way
examples: The conflict between management and workers makes for [[inefficiency]] in the workplace.

senses.en: become involved in an argument, fight, or other difficult situation in order to change what happens
examples: I don't usually like to [[intervene]] in disputes between husbands and wives.

senses.en: the act of becoming involved in an argument, fight, or other difficult situation in order to change what happens
examples: Repeated [[interventions]] on the currency markets have failed to prevent the value of the currency falling.

senses.zh: 有法律约束力的；必须遵守的
senses.en: that must be obeyed because it is accepted in law
examples: Participants in the world trade talks have agreed to negotiate specific [[binding]] commitments.

senses.en: sth. that encourages you to work harder, start a new activity, etc.
examples: There is little [[incentive]] for people to leave their cars at home when public transport remains so expensive.

senses.zh: 认为某事理所当然如此；认为某事是想当然（尤用于得出观点）
senses.en: accept that sth. is true or exists, esp. when you are developing an idea or argument
examples: The fact that people find change difficult is taken as a given.

senses.en: be involved in a plan, deal, etc.
examples: We need some financial advice — that's where Kate [[comes]] in.

senses.zh: 约翰 • 纳什（美国数学家）
罗素 • 克劳（澳大利亚演员）
亚当 • 斯密（苏格兰经济学家）
